title: Policy-as-code orchestration for residency/retention with drift detection & auto-evidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement a Policy-as-Code orchestration layer that compiles tenant-level data residency and retention requirements into enforceable runtime configs, continuously detects config drift across hosted/dedicated/private deployments, and automates generation of immutable evidence bundles for audit reporting. Goals: 1) Single source of truth for residency+retention policies (YAML/Jsonnet manifest authored by PMs/SEs). 2) Deterministic compilation to target enforcement primitives (S3 bucket region restrictions, database retention TTLs, ingestion routing policy, storage class rules, customer-level cache eviction settings). 3) Drift scanner that reconciles live config vs compiled policy and produces actionable drift findings with risk scoring. 4) Two remediation modes: a) Safe-apply (automated remediation for low-risk drifts with audit trail) and b) Manual workflow (create remediation task linked to customer workspace) for high-risk changes. 5) Evidence automation: periodic snapshot of policy, compiled artifacts, observed runtime state, remediation actions, and cryptographic attestations stored in an append-only evidence store for auditors. Scope: - Backend service (policy-hub) for policy storage, compilation, and versioning. - Reconciler service that performs continuous scans and emits findings to Console and to a compliance webhook. - Evidence exporter that packages audit bundles and uploads to an immutable S3 path and creates a PDF/CSV report summary. - Console UI surfaces: per-customer compliance timeline, outstanding drifts, remediation actions, and downloadable evidence bundles. Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end demo: create residency+retention policy for EU-only with 90-day retention, compile, and deploy to a test tenant; introduce a drift (simulate resource in us-east-1) and show detection, remediation flow, and evidence bundle generation. - Drift detection must show at least 95% precision on seeded test cases. - Evidence bundle must contain policy version, compiled artifact, observed state diff, remediation audit log, and cryptographic signature. - Automated remediation mode must be toggleable per-customer and logged with operator identity.

notes_for_engineering: Key decisions: use Jsonnet for policy authoring, produce an IR to decouple compilation from enforcement adapters, and sign evidence bundles with customer-specific KMS keys where available. Trade-offs: Jsonnet is more expressive but has steeper learning curve for PMs; will provide authoring templates and a small web editor in Console. Operational concerns: reconciler frequency tuned to avoid API burst limits (start with 1h scans for non-critical resources, 5m for retention TTLs).
risks: - Permission gaps when enumerating cross-account resources in Dedicated/Private deployments. - False positives from transient state during deployment windows; need suppression windows. - Evidence storage costs if bundles are large; will support configurable bundle granularity.

audit_checklist: policy manifest versioned in policy-hub git store
compiled artifact stored with SHA and timestamp
drift finding includes observed state and expected state diff
remediation action recorded with operator identity and timestamp
evidence bundle contains signed manifest and remediation log
implementation_notes: Adapters will be implemented as small modules: s3-enforcer, db-ttl-enforcer, routing-enforcer, lifecycle-enforcer. Each adapter exposes dry-run and apply endpoints. The reconciler will call adapters in dry-run to surface potential changes and optionally call apply for safe-apply mode. Use event-sourcing for audit trail: append-only events stored in dedicated compliance-events topic. Consider using existing Optimize caching hints to avoid scanning cold tenants frequently.
